glosses: go on, keep going, continue to do something

examples.text: Die Linke braucht dringend neue Köpfe und eine Kursänderung. Und die Parteichefin? Will weitermachen. Damit sabotiert sie den Neuanfang.
examples.translation: (Le parti) la gauche a besoin de toute urgence de nouvelles têtes et d’un changement de cap. Et la présidente du parti ? Elle veut continuer. Elle sabote ainsi le nouveau départ.

glosses: To talk frequently or at great length (about a subject).

examples.text: Will you stop going on about your stupid holiday?
Sam goes on and on about Pokémon.
Don't ask Sam about Pokémon, because he'll go on and on.

"I don't believe you." I shake my head. "How on earth did you remember that? I must have told you years ago."[…]
"First of all, you go on about it far more than you think you do,[…]."
What's going on?

glosses: To move or proceed so as to become \"on\" in any of various senses.

examples.text: Bertha's about to finish her song. Who's going on next?
Smith went on for Jones at left back after Jones got injured.
It was pitch black and then suddenly all the lights went on.

glosses: Expressing that the speaker can continue speaking without interruption from the listener.

examples.text: Go on! You were saying about those other ones too?

A: He asked Fiona to marry him.
B: Go on!
A: It's true, I swear.
Go on! You can do it!

—So three hundred on the chair then, and can we do two-fifty on the clock?
—Go on, then.

glosses: To use and adopt (information) in order to understand an issue, make a decision, etc.; to go by.

examples.text: We can't go on what this map says; it's twenty years out of date.
I didn't make a decision because I didn't have anything to go on.
The grandfather clock keeps going for over a week without winding.

glosses: To proceed; to make progress, physically or figuratively.

examples.text: The Gunners have never gone out of the FA Cup in the third round under Arsene Wenger and never lost to a lower division side, two impressive runs they kept going at Elland Road on an evening that was fraught with potential dangers.

glosses: To see that (a person) is continually supplied with something, or that they can progress or carry on.

examples.text: I didn't think I could run any longer, but fear kept me going.
I'll put all this meat in my freezer, and it'll keep me going for many months.
[…] he was generous when he had the cash. Many a time he kept me going in drink through the week when I was stuck for the ready […]

glosses: To proceed with (doing an activity); to prolong (an activity).

examples.text: Shall I continue speaking, or will you just interrupt me again?
Do you want me to continue to unload these?

glosses: To retain (someone or something) in a given state, position, etc.

examples.text: […] dip the mouth of it within the second glass and remove your finger; continue it in that posture for a time, and it will unmingle the wine from the water […]

glosses: To remain in a given place or condition; to remain in connection with; to abide; to stay.

examples.text: Here to continue, and build up here / A growing empire.

examples.text: Moreover, where three lives and a sparse availability of extra life-giving '1-Ups' marked the 1991 experience, the iPod player is offered an unlimited number of continues with which to progress through the gameworld.

glosses: Prolonger à quelqu’un la possession de quelque chose.

examples.text: Continuez-lui vos bienfaits.

examples.text: On le continua dans son commandement, dans son gouvernement.
